terms.definition: Detection of deviations from ambient temperature, usually using a device that measures or records temperature changes.
Activity, evidence, or conditions that differ from what is expected and have not yet been explained.
The perception of meaningful patterns, connections, or significance in unrelated or random information.
A visual phenomenon interpreted as a person, figure, animal, object, or presence that is not ordinarily visible or physically accounted for at the time of observation.
The reported appearance of an object without an immediately identified physical source.
The reported disappearance of an object without an immediately identified physical cause.
The idea that paranormal activity can be connected or attached to a person, place, object, or presence.
A category of phenomena involving any auditory event that is perceived or documented.
The perception or interpretation of unclear or ambiguous audio as meaningful sound or language.
A perceived field of energy surrounding a person, place, or object, sometimes represented as a glow.
An initial measurement or observation recorded before an investigation or controlled test, used as a comparison point to help identify anomalies or changes in conditions.
An unexpected loss of battery charge that may be interpreted as anomalous activity or as evidence of it.
Describes reported activity or presence perceived as helpful, protective, harmless, or positive in intent.
A practice in which a book or written text is opened and a page, word, or passage is selected at random and interpreted for significance.
A technique that prompts for a response, frequently by asking a question or making a noise, then monitors for a response.
Motion-activated light-up balls, often sold as pet toys, used during investigations as visible indicators of movement or vibration.
Documentation of how evidence was collected, handled, stored, and reviewed.
An event or perception reported by more than one person, either at the same time or in close sequence, and interpreted as involving the same anomalous activity, presence, or phenomenon.
Evidence affected by environmental contamination, handling, instrument error, or other conditions that make it unreliable or unsuitable for analysis.
A known or intentionally arranged condition used to help distinguish reported anomalous activity from ordinary environmental, technical, psychological, or procedural explanations.
Evidence from another witness or source that supports or aligns with a report or other evidence.
A device used to record multiple measurements or environmental conditions over time for later review.
The process of disproving a claim that specific activity, evidence, or an experience is or was paranormal in origin.
A presence believed or interpreted to be nonhuman or spiritual, commonly associated with harmful, hostile, deceptive, or malevolent intent.
A voice-like or speech-like sound heard at the time it occurs without an apparent source.
Handheld rods believed to sometimes indicate paranormal activity by moving, crossing, or pointing.

Historically, a substance claimed in mediumship to appear during spirit communication; in modern investigations, also used for web-like or fibrous material found at a location and interpreted as possible paranormal evidence.

In supernatural investigation, a measurement used to document variances in electromagnetic radiation. These variances can be interpreted as possible evidence of paranormal activity when considered alongside the full investigation context.
Recorded audio interpreted as an anomalous sound, signal, voice, or noise that was not observed at the time of recording.
Recorded audio interpreted as voices or speech that were otherwise not observed at the time of recording.
A device used to measure electromagnetic fields or changes in electromagnetic field strength.
A sudden or notable increase in an EMF reading during an investigation that may be interpreted as possible evidence of paranormal activity.
A commonly used term for describing or explaining a wide variety of anomalous activity.
An environmental condition or factor that may affect, distort, or inhibit analysis of reported or recorded activity.
A technique in which a listener wearing headphones is isolated from outside visual and auditory cues and speaks words or sounds they hear from an audio-generating device such as a spirit box.
A ritual or practice intended to remove, expel, or separate a spirit, entity, or other nonphysical presence from a person, place, or object.

A scenario in which a person believes they have awakened, often in a familiar setting, before later realizing they were still asleep; unusual events during the experience may be interpreted as paranormal activity.
Evidence that appears to indicate anomalous activity but is later explained by ordinary causes.
Sounds believed to be footsteps that are heard or recorded without an immediately identifiable source.
A common term for unexplained activity interpreted as involving a person, animal, object, place, or presence that is not ordinarily observable.

A location where the surrounding landscape creates the visual impression that a slight downhill slope is uphill, making vehicles or objects appear to roll against gravity; these sites are sometimes associated with ghost stories or mistaken for paranormal activity.
A pattern of unexplained activity associated with a person, place, or object.
A transitional state between wakefulness and sleep in which vivid sensory experiences, imagery, sounds, or feelings may occur and sometimes be interpreted as paranormal activity.
Sounds heard or recorded that resemble familiar object-based sounds, such as doors closing or furniture moving, when the associated objects are not present or cannot be identified.
The idea that energy, emotion, activity, or significant events can linger in a place, environment, object, or person and later be experienced as anomalous or paranormal activity.
A camera that records infrared light, used to document visual information outside normal visible-light conditions.
Sound below the usual lower limit of human hearing that has been known to cause physical symptoms, including discomfort, unease, vibration, or other reported experiences.
The use of devices, usually electronic, to attempt communication in the context of paranormal activity.
Unexplained activity interpreted as showing awareness, intention, or purposeful behavior.
A type of phenomena involving apparent movement, force, vibration, or disturbance of physical objects.
Knocks, taps, bangs, or similar impact-like sounds that are heard or recorded without an immediately identifiable source.
A projected pattern of laser points or lines, or the device that produces it, used as a visible reference for detecting movement or visual disturbances.
An experience in which a person perceives that an unexplained gap, delay, or discontinuity occurred in their awareness or memory.
Describes reported activity or presence perceived as harmful, threatening, hostile, or negative in intent.
A perceived expression of anomalous or paranormal activity, including sensory, environmental, visual, audio, or physical phenomena.
A manifestation in which a person, figure, object, substance, or physical form is perceived as appearing or becoming visible.
A phenomenon in which a voice, sound, or noise is perceived as resembling a specific person, animal, object, or source that is not present or cannot be identified.
Visible haze, vapor, smoke, fog-like forms, or clouded areas witnessed in person or seen in images.
A presence believed or interpreted as spiritual, nonphysical, or entity-like without being identified as formerly human.
Circular or spherical forms, usually light-emitting and sometimes dark, seen in photographs, video, or direct observation.
A board or similar surface marked with letters, numbers, and other indicators, used with a planchette or pointer in attempts to receive messages or responses.
A broad term for something that appears to fall outside ordinary explanation based on the information currently available.
Media, events, performances, or commercial content centered on paranormal or haunted subjects for entertainment purposes.
Travel, visitation, or public interest associated with places known, believed, or promoted as having paranormal or haunted significance.
Organized visits or guided experiences centered on places presented as paranormal, haunted, or historically associated with unusual activity.
The study of claimed psi-related experiences and abilities, such as telepathy, clairvoyance, precognition, psychokinesis, and survival-related claims.
The perception of meaningful patterns, faces, figures, words, or voices in ambiguous or random sensory information.
A firsthand account of an event directly experienced by an individual that lacks corroborating evidence.
Odors perceived without an immediately identifiable source, commonly including smoke, perfume, or other distinctive smells.
A category of phenomena involving changes in physical objects, substances, or environmental conditions, such as movement, marks, odors, or temperature shifts.
A category of phenomena involving physical sensations or symptoms interpreted as paranormal in origin, such as headaches, dizziness, chills, goosebumps, nausea, pressure, or fatigue.
A type of anomalous activity commonly associated with physical disturbances such as object movement, knocking or banging sounds, or other physical events.
The idea that a place or location can act as a passage or access point for paranormal activity, spirits, entities, or other nonphysical presences.
A state in which a person is believed or interpreted to be influenced, controlled, or inhabited by a spirit, entity, or other nonphysical presence.
A technique that uses confrontational, challenging, or emotionally charged statements in an attempt to elicit a response.
Writing or written marks produced while a person holds a pen, pencil, marker, or other writing instrument and reports that they are not consciously moving it.
Unexplained activity that appears to repeat in a similar way over time without apparent awareness, intention, or purposeful behavior.
A device that emits an electromagnetic field from its antenna and detects changes to that field, often producing lights or sounds when changes are detected.
Scratches or marks on the skin that cannot immediately be explained and may be interpreted as evidence of paranormal activity.

A condition in which conflicting sensory cues, such as uneven floors, sloped surfaces, low ceilings, visual distortion, or unusual spatial layout, may cause physical sensations and/or emotional responses.
A technique that limits sensory input, commonly sight and/or hearing, in an attempt to reduce outside awareness and increase focus on selected sensations, impressions, or perceptions.
A common term for dark, shadow-like figures perceived as human-shaped or presence-like, commonly lacking clear features or seen briefly, peripherally, or under low-light conditions.
A temporary state near sleep or waking in which a person is aware but unable to move, sometimes accompanied by vivid dreamlike perceptions that may be interpreted as paranormal activity.
A camera system that uses projected infrared light points and software to interpret human-shaped forms, often displaying them as stick figures.
A presence believed or interpreted as nonphysical and as continuing after physical life.
A device that rapidly scans radio frequencies or audio channels to generate sounds that may be interpreted as communication or other anomalous content.
The tendency for expectations or context to influence perception or interpretation.
A broad term for phenomena interpreted as existing beyond the known laws of nature or not fully explained by them.
Reported or measured shifts in ambient temperature, surface temperature, or perceived heat or cold, commonly referred to as cold spots or hot spots.
A camera that detects infrared radiation and displays or records temperature differences as an image.
A meter commonly used to detect or measure AC magnetic fields, AC electric fields, and RF or microwave signals.
An object used in an attempt to elicit or encourage paranormal activity.
A category of phenomena involving any visual event that is witnessed in person or documented in images or video.
Low-volume voice-like or speech-like sounds heard or recorded without an apparent source.
A device or application that selects words, sounds, or phrases from a precompiled list and produces or displays them for review as potentially meaningful output.
